name: Ponytail face lift

card.summary: Two related things: a surgical "Ponytail Lift" that mimics a high-ponytail vertical lift with hidden incisions, and the hair-pulled-back look used as a temporary facial lift.
card.note: The surgical version is an operation; the hairstyle version is temporary.

quick.overview:
The ponytail face lift refers to a tight high ponytail that pulls skin up and back, giving a temporary lifted look often called an "instalift". It also names an endoscopic surgical technique that simulates the same vertical lift.

The surgical Ponytail Lift is described in a 2023 Clinics in Plastic Surgery review of Asian facial rejuvenation, using minimally invasive methods with hidden incisions.
quick.how: The hairstyle version is a high, tight ponytail or bun styled to draw the face upward. The surgical version is performed by a surgeon.
quick.risks: A tight ponytail can cause scalp tension or traction on hair. Surgery carries standard operative risks.

lead: The ponytail face lift has two uses. As a styling trick it is a high, tight ponytail that draws the skin of the face upward, sometimes called an instalift.

As surgery, the "Ponytail Lift" is a technique described by authors of a 2023 Clinics in Plastic Surgery review on endoscopic Asian facial rejuvenation; it is designed to simulate the vertical lift of the face when the hair is pulled into a high ponytail.[1]

The authors say traditional SMAS face lifts were developed on white patients and may not meet aesthetic goals of Asian patients, and that ideal techniques use hidden incisions to avoid hypertrophic scarring and cultural stigma.[1]

chain: Hair pulled up in high ponytail
angle.text: A tight high ponytail visibly lifts the brow and cheeks while worn. The surgical technique aims for a similar vertical lift that persists.

paras: The technique is presented within a minimally invasive approach combining endoscopic methods with skin regenerative methods, aiming to lift vertically while hiding incisions.[1]
The hairstyle version needs no products; it is a temporary effect that ends when the hair is released.
No studies found. The technique is described in a review article rather than a controlled trial.[1]

timeline.event: Ponytail Lift described in Clinics in Plastic Surgery review.[1]
